query: Micron consumer SSD and PC smartphone memory revenue
normalized: consumer memory micron pc revenue smartphone ssd

output.content:
Micron does **not publicly disclose separate revenue** for consumer SSDs, PC memory, and smartphone memory; its closest reported bucket is the **Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU)**, which aggregates mobile and client products rather than providing an end-market/product revenue split. In fiscal Q4 2026, MCBU revenue was a record **$13.114 billion**, versus **$11.521 billion** in Q3 2026 and **$3.760 billion** in Q4 2025. [[1]] 

For context, Micron reported total fiscal-2026 revenue of **$133.188 billion**, so Q4 MCBU represented approximately **24%** of company revenue; management said the quarter’s MCBU increase was driven by higher pricing, partly offset by lower bit shipments. [[1]] [[2]]

**What can be said by category:**
- **PC memory and client SSDs:** These are included in MCBU, but Micron does not publish their individual revenue. Micron said PC and mobile demand was concentrated in premium devices, with AI-enabled PCs and smartphones requiring more DRAM and NAND content. [[2]]
- **Smartphone memory:** Smartphone DRAM and NAND are likewise included in MCBU rather than separately disclosed. Micron reported it was shipping its 6-channel 1-gamma LPDDR5X for flagship mobile devices in fiscal Q4 2026. [[1]]
- **Consumer SSDs / Crucial:** Micron announced on December 3, 2025 that it would exit the Crucial consumer business—including consumer-branded products sold through retailers, e-tailers, and distributors—and would continue channel shipments only through the end of fiscal Q2 2026. Consequently, consumer SSD revenue should no longer be viewed as a continuing standalone growth category after that transition. [[3]]
- **SSD revenue disclosed separately:** The only SSD subcategory Micron quantified was **data-center SSD revenue**, which was nearly **$10 billion** in fiscal Q4 2026 and more than two-thirds of company NAND revenue; that figure is distinct from consumer and client SSDs. [[2]] 

At the technology level, Micron generated **$100.7 billion of DRAM revenue** and **$31.8 billion of NAND revenue** in fiscal 2026, but these technology totals span data center, PC, smartphone, automotive, embedded, and other applications and therefore cannot be used to isolate PC or smartphone revenue. [[2]]
